description:
## The gap

Elixir's `## Examples` blocks are doctests: `mix test` runs them, so an example that stops being true fails the build. fz has no equivalent. A doc example is prose, checked once by whoever wrote it and never again.

This session has already found three runtime-library comments that described code which no longer existed -- case mapping claimed to be ASCII-only when it was full Unicode, `String.Chars` claiming fz had no interpolation, `String`'s header miscounting its own primitives. Every one of them was written true and went stale silently. Doc examples are the same hazard with a sharper edge, because an example looks like evidence.

## What exists to build on

`fz2 test <src.fz>` already discovers and runs `test(:name) do ... end`, one subprocess per test, with `--interp` to route through the backend interpreter. The oracle harness already proves fz output against an Elixir twin. Neither reads doc comments.

## Shape

Extract each `## Examples` block from a `@doc`, pair each indented call with the `#=>` line under it, and emit a check that the call renders to that value. Two plausible homes:

- A fixture the matrix already runs, generated from the library sources, so a stale example fails on every door.
- A `fz2 doctest` subcommand over the same discovery `fz2 test` uses.

The first is cheaper and inherits the four-path guarantee for free.

## Until then

Examples are verified by hand at the time they are written, by running the call and copying the rendered value. That is a real check, but it is a check with no ratchet.
title: Nothing executes the examples in runtime-library doc comments
